title: Request Lifecycle
markdown:
A single chat message makes a full round-trip through the API, the orchestrator's tool-use loop, a parallel specialist fan-out, and synthesis — all streamed back as server-sent events.

### Steps

1. **Arrival** — the client posts to `POST /chat` (`openexecutive.api.routes.chat`). The turn carries a `<current_speaker>` hint resolved from the caller's `person_id`, plus a `<briefing>` digest of current open alerts (built in parallel with RAG/episodic/peer-memory fetches) so the Executive can discuss any item shown on the `/today` briefing page A turn arriving from a chat adapter instead of the web app also carries a `<channel>` block naming the surface and stating which approvals can be completed there; on Slack the `<briefing>` digest is gated to the principal's DMs. All three ride in the **user turn**, never a cached system block.
2. **Routing pre-pass** — before the full tool surface is shown at all, the Executive makes one call offering `consult_specialist` and nothing else (`ROUTING_PREPASS_ENABLED`, on by default). On the full surface that tool competes with ~58 other client tools and a smaller model does not reach for it: measured on a local 27B model, a strategic sequencing question consulted on 1 of 12 turns with the full surface and 9-11 of 12 across two runs with the pre-pass plus the persona's consulting section. Whatever it picks is dispatched immediately through the same `route_parallel` fan-out and replayed into the conversation as a matching tool_use/tool_result pair. A pre-pass that picks nobody appends nothing, so a turn that just wants an action taken is unaffected.
3. **Tool-use loop** — the `Executive` calls Claude, with the full tool surface and with any pre-pass findings already in the conversation. For a cross-domain question the assistant turn emits multiple `consult_specialist` tool-use blocks at once.
4. **Parallel fan-out** — `openexecutive.orchestrator.router.route_parallel` dispatches those calls concurrently, bounded by `MAX_PARALLEL_SPECIALISTS`; calls past the cap get a skip tool_result.
5. **Per-specialist RAG** — each specialist runs its own domain-filtered ChromaDB query, then reasons over the retrieved chunks and returns analysis as a tool_result.
6. **Synthesis** — the Executive feeds the tool_results back to Claude and streams one coherent reply; a `thinking` keepalive covers the specialist round.
7. **Optional committee review** — when enabled, `Executive.stream_chat_with_committee()` runs a silent draft, parallel reviewer critiques, then a streamed revision pass.
8. **Side effects** — any side-effecting tool call surfaces an `action_taken` chip; the stream closes with a `done` event. One side-effecting tool is gated server-side rather than by its description: `ack_alert` will only accept an `alert_id` from the live alert board the server itself derived this turn — the whole live set, not only the rows the `<briefing>` digest printed, since `/today` renders more cards than the digest lists and every one of them is Discuss-able — and it fails closed, so an id it cannot even parse is refused rather than waved through to the handler's own parse. That check runs on **every** session. It used to run only on turns that arrived from a chat channel, keyed on `origin_channel`, which the browser never sets — so the web, the surface the principal actually uses, was unchecked and the model could ack any id, including one quoted out of an alert body by the briefing page's Discuss handoff. What that buys is bounded and worth stating plainly: an id that is invented, closed, snoozed or expired is refused, including one quoted out of an attacker-written alert body; the model being argued into acking the wrong *live* card is not prevented. A session that was shown no board has an empty trusted set and can ack nothing, so the unattended passes (the nightly reflection, the research synthesis) are now refused by default — they also still withhold the tool outright, which is belt-and-braces rather than the only thing stopping them. After the stream closes, the turn is also handed to the episodic memory extractor (`memory.episodic.schedule_extraction`, fire-and-forget) — on every turn where the principal said anything at all, and only the principal: a turn naming an `origin_channel` must resolve to a person marked `is_principal`, because the quote validator downstream cannot tell whose words it is checking. Both this path and the committee path call the same `should_extract` predicate, and it applies no length floor: the gate used to sum in the assistant's reply, which let a verbose answer drag a trivial turn in and discarded the short, decisive instructions that are the whole point of extracting. A user-side floor would fare no better — "Do B." and "Done" are one character apart. See **Memory** for what that cost on a live tenant.
9. **Tool failures** — a handler that raises instead of returning its JSON error is isolated: both tool gathers run with `return_exceptions=True`, the model gets an error `tool_result` naming only the exception's TYPE — a message can carry a filesystem path, a validation error echoing the input, or a third-party HTTP body, and anything in model context can be quoted back to the user, so the full repr stays in the log and the audit row — and the failure is audited with `ok=false`. Only `CancelledError` is re-raised, so turn-timeout and client-disconnect handling still work. Before this one crashing tool aborted the whole turn, which reached the user as an unexplained apology with no audit row (#136).

Web search takes one of two shapes, decided per call by `select_web_search_tool(model)` against the model the request is actually sent with. On the Anthropic path it executes inside the Anthropic API itself (`web_search_20250305`) and returns within the same generation; for any model routed via OpenRouter the same tool becomes OpenRouter's `openrouter:web_search` server tool, which also runs inside the generation with the same search cap and domain lists. For a slug in `LOCAL_MODELS` there is no server tool to use, so with `SEARXNG_URL` set the Executive offers a client-side `web_search` tool instead: the model emits an ordinary `tool_use` block, the handler queries SearXNG in-process, and the results return as a `tool_result` on the next iteration — one extra round trip per search, unlike the server path. A failed search comes back with error wording the model can tell apart from an empty result (the Anthropic `is_error` flag is set too, but the OpenAI-compatible translator does not forward it), and every result set is wrapped in a notice marking it as untrusted third-party text, never instructions. Searches are capped per turn by a budget created once before the tool-use loop.
mermaid:
sequenceDiagram
  participant C as Client
  participant API as FastAPI /chat
  participant E as Executive
  participant CL as Claude
  participant S as Specialists
  participant KB as ChromaDB
  C->>API: POST /chat message
  API->>E: start turn
  E->>CL: messages (tool-use loop)
  CL-->>E: consult_specialist calls
  E->>S: route_parallel fan-out
  S->>KB: domain-filtered RAG
  KB-->>S: chunks
  S-->>E: analysis tool_results
  E->>CL: synthesize
  CL-->>E: streamed reply
  E-->>API: SSE chunks then done
  API-->>C: streamed response
